title: Rational and radical functions
purpose: Understand excluded inputs, discontinuities, sign changes, and inverse relationships before calculus.

lessons.title: Holes, asymptotes, and intercepts
lessons.objective: Identify original domain exclusions, removable holes, vertical asymptotes, intercepts, and end behavior of a rational function.
lessons.coverage: Factor cancellation with retained exclusions, denominator zeros, horizontal and slant asymptotes, and the fact that a graph can cross a horizontal asymptote.
lessons.activity: Compare an original rational expression and its reduced form, including a table row at a canceled root and a graph with an explicit open point.
families: Construct a rational function with specified holes and poles
Classify horizontal/slant behavior using degrees or division
lessons.generatorRules: Generate numerator and denominator from known factors; track the original denominator separately. Include canceled and uncanceled factors and equal-degree cases.
lessons.commonError: Turning every denominator zero into an asymptote or restoring a canceled input to the domain.
lessons.feedback: Contrast an undefined original value with a nearby trend and identify which denominator factors remain after reduction.
lessons.checkpoint: Domain, hole-versus-pole classification, intercepts, and end behavior.

lessons.title: Polynomial and rational inequalities
lessons.objective: Build a sign chart and return every interval satisfying a polynomial or rational inequality.
lessons.coverage: Critical values from numerator and denominator, multiplicity effects, interval test points, and different endpoint rules for zeros and exclusions.
lessons.activity: Partition a number line at critical values, predict signs on each interval, then test one value per interval and assemble the solution set.
families: Solve factored polynomial inequalities with repeated roots
Solve rational inequalities with excluded boundaries
lessons.generatorRules: Use ordered rational critical values and include repeated factors. Never multiply across an inequality by a variable expression without accounting for its sign.
lessons.commonError: Multiplying by an unknown-sign denominator or including a pole in a non-strict solution.
lessons.feedback: Offer a test input from a misclassified interval and separate numerator-zero and denominator-zero endpoint rules.
lessons.checkpoint: A polynomial inequality, a rational inequality, an endpoint decision, and an invalid-step explanation.

lessons.title: Variation and rational models
lessons.objective: Build a direct, inverse, or joint variation model and use units and restrictions to interpret a result.
lessons.coverage: Proportionality constants, inverse-square relationships, combined variation, solving for a parameter, and distinguishing mathematical from physical domains.
lessons.activity: Compare a model prediction after doubling one input with a parameter table; explain why an inverse relationship halves the output rather than subtracting a constant.
families: Recover a variation constant from one calibration observation
Predict the effect of an input scale change or solve a constrained rational model
lessons.generatorRules: Keep physical lengths and resistances positive; supply the model so prior physics knowledge is unnecessary. Reject zero-denominator and physically invalid solutions explicitly.
lessons.commonError: Replacing inverse variation with a negative linear slope or applying a physical model outside its allowed interval.
lessons.feedback: Use an input ratio and output ratio before substituting numbers; inspect units on the recovered constant.
lessons.checkpoint: Direct, inverse, joint variation, and a domain-limited application.

lessons.title: Radical functions and restricted inverses
lessons.objective: Analyze a radical function's domain and range and verify an inverse on the correct restricted domain.
lessons.coverage: Even and odd roots, horizontal and vertical transformations, square-root principal branch, solving for an inverse, and checking both input and output restrictions.
lessons.activity: Reflect a restricted quadratic and a square-root graph across y=x, then test a point outside the permitted branch using their tables.
families: Determine domain and range of transformed root functions
Match a restricted power function with its valid inverse
lessons.generatorRules: Record branch restrictions as part of the expected answer. Include negative shifts and one odd-root comparison without requiring complex-valued functions.
lessons.commonError: Treating a square-root function as both positive and negative branches or declaring a full quadratic one-to-one.
lessons.feedback: Ask which output the function actually assigns and return to the horizontal-line test in m02-l03.
lessons.checkpoint: Domain, range, a restricted inverse, and a composition check at a boundary.

anchor.answer: r(x)=x+1 only for x!=1, with a hole at (1,2). The inequality solution is (-infinity,-1) union [2,infinity); -1 is excluded.

moduleExit: A learner must preserve exclusions while moving among original formulas, reduced formulas, sign charts, and graphs.
